situation: Disagreeing with your manager's plan
mightSay: Sir, your plan is wrong, it will not work at all.
better: I see the goal. I'm worried the timeline is too tight for testing.
changes: name the concern, not the person

next.title: Offer a way forward

lines.label: Suggest
lines.text: Could we keep the plan and add one more week for testing?

next.note: Bring an option, not just a problem.

situation: Saying no to weekend work
mightSay: I can't come on weekend, I have some personal work.
better: I can't work this weekend. I can start early on Monday instead.

next.title: If it's urgent

lines.label: Option
lines.text: If it can't wait, I can give it one hour on Sunday evening.

next.note: A firm no with an option still sounds helpful.

situation: Asking a senior to review your work
mightSay: Please check my work once and tell me if anything is wrong.
better: Could you review the pricing section by Thursday? I'm least sure about the discounts.

next.title: Make it easy

lines.label: Add
lines.text: It's two pages. Ten minutes should be enough.

next.note: Busy people say yes to small, clear asks.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining what an app update does
mightSay: We have done some backend optimisations and UI enhancements in the new build.
better: The new version opens faster and the buttons are easier to find.

next.title: Add one example

lines.label: Example
lines.text: Your order history now loads in one second, not five.

next.note: Describe the change from their side of the screen.

situation: Disagreeing in a group chat
mightSay: No no, this is totally wrong, everyone please listen to me.
better: I see it a bit differently. Can I share one point before we decide?

next.title: Move it to a call

lines.label: Suggest
lines.text: Happy to explain on a quick call if that's easier.

next.note: Long disagreements go better outside the group.

situation: Saying no to a friend who wants a loan
mightSay: Actually right now I am having some tight situation, so it will be difficult.
better: I'm sorry, I can't lend money right now.

next.title: Still help

lines.label: Offer
lines.text: I can't lend it, but I can help you look at other options.

next.note: You don't owe a reason for saying no to a loan.

situation: Asking IT to fix your laptop
mightSay: My laptop is not working properly, please do something urgently.
better: My laptop freezes every time I open Excel. Could someone look at it today?

next.title: Give the details

lines.label: Details
lines.text: It started after yesterday's update. The error says 'not responding'.

next.note: The more exact you are, the faster the fix.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a bug to a client
mightSay: There was one small bug in the code which got introduced in last deployment.
better: Since Tuesday's update, some invoices showed the wrong total. We've fixed it.

next.title: Say what's next

lines.label: Next
lines.text: We've corrected those invoices and added a check so it won't happen again.

next.note: Clients want the impact and the fix, not the code.

situation: Saying you'll reply later, without 'revert'
mightSay: I will revert back to you by evening.
better: I'll get back to you by this evening.

next.title: Even better

lines.label: Specific
lines.text: I'll send you the numbers by 6 p.m. today.

next.note: Outside India, 'revert' means 'undo', not 'reply'.

situation: Disagreeing with a client's idea
mightSay: Sir, this idea will not work, we have tried before only.
better: That could work. When we tried something similar, sign-ups dropped, so I'd test it small first.

next.title: Make it their choice

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: Would you like us to try it in one city first?

next.note: Clients accept a test more easily than a no.

situation: Saying no to a wedding invite
mightSay: I will try my best to come but I am not sure, so many things are there.
better: Thank you so much for inviting me. I'm sorry, I won't be able to make it.

next.title: Show you care

lines.label: Add
lines.text: I'd love to see the photos, and I'll call you that week.

next.note: A clear no is kinder than a maybe they wait on.

situation: Asking a colleague to cover a meeting
mightSay: Can you attend my 3 o'clock meeting, I am busy.
better: Could you cover my 3 p.m. client call? I'll send you the notes and the two open points.

next.title: Thank them

lines.label: Return
lines.text: Thanks, I owe you one. Happy to cover one of yours next week.

next.note: Make the favour small and offer one back.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining the cloud to a parent
mightSay: Cloud means data is stored in remote servers which are accessed over internet.
better: Your photos are kept on the company's computers, so you can see them on any phone.

next.title: Answer the worry

lines.label: Reassure
lines.text: If your phone is lost, the photos are still there.

next.note: Start from what they use, not how it works.

situation: Disagreeing with a friend's restaurant pick
mightSay: That place is very bad, I am not coming there.
better: I'm not keen on that one. How about the new place near the station?

next.title: Keep it easy

lines.label: Add
lines.text: But if everyone wants your pick, I'm in.

next.note: With friends, a light touch keeps the plan fun.

situation: Saying no to a client's extra request
mightSay: This is out of scope, we cannot do it.
better: That isn't part of this phase. I can send a quote to add it.
changes: turn the no into an option

next.title: Give a date

lines.label: Option
lines.text: Or we can add it to phase two, starting in March.

next.note: A paid option protects the work and the client.

situation: Asking a friend to help you move house
mightSay: You are free on Sunday, right? Come to my place, we are shifting.
better: I'm moving house on Sunday. Could you help for a couple of hours in the morning?

next.title: Make it worth it

lines.label: Offer
lines.text: Lunch is on me, and I'll help when you move.

next.note: A clear time makes it easy to say yes.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining why a website is slow
mightSay: Website is slow due to heavy payload and less server capacity.
better: The pages have large pictures, and too many people visit at once. Both slow it down.

next.title: Say the fix

lines.label: Fix
lines.text: Smaller pictures and a bigger plan will make it twice as fast.

next.note: Pair each cause with what you'll do about it.

situation: Disagreeing with a parent about a big purchase
mightSay: Papa, you don't understand, this car is not good.
better: I can see why you like it. I'm worried about the running cost. Can we compare two more?

next.title: Bring facts

lines.label: Facts
lines.text: This one costs about ₹3,000 more a month in fuel.

next.note: Numbers keep the talk calm.

situation: Saying no to a last-minute meeting
mightSay: I cannot join, I already have so many calls today.
better: I can't make it at 4 today. Could we do 11 tomorrow?

next.title: Stay in the loop

lines.label: Option
lines.text: If it has to be today, please send me the notes and I'll reply by evening.

next.note: Offer a path so the work still moves.

situation: Asking for help with a tool you don't know
mightSay: I don't know this software at all, please teach me everything.
better: I'm new to Jira. Could you show me how to create and assign a ticket?

next.title: Ask for a time

lines.label: Time
lines.text: Ten minutes after lunch would be enough.

next.note: A small, specific ask gets a quick yes.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining data privacy to a relative
mightSay: Data privacy means your PII should not be shared with third parties without consent.
better: Apps collect your name, number and location. Privacy means they can't share it without asking you.

next.title: Give one tip

lines.label: Tip
lines.text: Before you tap 'Allow', ask: does this app really need my location?

next.note: One habit is more useful than the rules.

situation: Disagreeing with the meeting's conclusion
mightSay: I don't agree with what everyone decided, it is not correct.
better: Before we close, I have one concern about the budget. Can I raise it?

next.title: Say it in one line

lines.label: Concern
lines.text: The plan needs ₹5 lakh, but we only approved ₹3 lakh.

next.note: One fact moves a room more than a long speech.

situation: Saying no to lending your car
mightSay: Actually my car has some issue, and my father also needs it, so...
better: I'm sorry, I don't lend my car. I hope you find one.

next.title: Help another way

lines.label: Offer
lines.text: I can drop you at the station on Saturday, if that helps.

next.note: A rule is easier to say than a new excuse every time.

situation: Asking your manager for more people
mightSay: We are short of resources, please give more resources.
better: To launch by June, we need one more developer. Without one, we'd slip to August.
changes: link the ask to the goal

next.title: Offer a choice

lines.label: Choice
lines.text: Or we can launch in June with two fewer features.

next.note: Give your manager a decision, not a complaint.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining what a database is
mightSay: Database is a structured collection of data stored electronically.
better: A database is where the app keeps its lists: customers, orders and prices.

next.title: Show it

lines.label: Example
lines.text: When you search for an order, the app looks it up in the database.

next.note: One real moment beats a definition.

situation: Disagreeing when you're the junior person
mightSay: Sorry, I may be wrong, I am very junior, but maybe this is not right?
better: Can I share a concern? The test data shows a different result.

next.title: Ask a question

lines.label: Question
lines.text: Could we check the numbers again before we send it?

next.note: A question lets you disagree without fighting rank.

situation: Saying no to a relative's job favour
mightSay: Uncle, I will see what I can do, I will try.
better: I can't recommend him for the role, but I can share the job link.

next.title: Keep it warm

lines.label: Add
lines.text: I'm happy to look at his CV and give him tips.

next.note: 'I'll try' is a promise you may not keep.

situation: Asking a stranger for directions
mightSay: Hello, metro station is where?
better: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the metro station?

next.title: Check you got it

lines.label: Repeat
lines.text: So, left at the bank, then straight on? Thank you!

next.note: Saying it back saves a wrong turn.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a dashboard to the sales team
mightSay: This dashboard shows KPIs and metrics with filters for drill-down analysis.
better: This page shows your sales this week, who's ahead, and which deals are stuck.

next.title: Show the first click

lines.label: Start
lines.text: Each morning, look at the 'Stuck deals' box first.

next.note: Tell them what to do with it, not just what it is.

situation: Disagreeing with feedback you got
mightSay: That is not true, I did all the work properly.
better: Thanks for the feedback. Could you share an example? I'd like to understand it.

next.title: Then give your side

lines.label: Your view
lines.text: On the March report, I used the template we agreed. Should that change?

next.note: Understand first, then explain.

situation: Saying no to a second helping
mightSay: No no, I cannot eat more, please don't give.
better: It was delicious, thank you. I'm really full.

next.title: If they insist

lines.label: Again
lines.text: I'd love to, but I really can't. Could I take some home?

next.note: Praise makes the no feel kind.

situation: Asking for help when you're stuck
mightSay: I am stuck since morning, nothing is working.
better: I've been stuck on the login error for two hours. Could you take a look?

next.title: Show what you tried

lines.label: Tried
lines.text: I've cleared the cache and checked the keys. Neither fixed it.

next.note: Saying what you tried saves their time.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining why a small change takes a week
mightSay: It looks small but actually there are many dependencies in the code.
better: The button is small, but it touches payments, so we have to test every way to pay.

next.title: Break down the week

lines.label: Plan
lines.text: Two days to build, three days to test.

next.note: A breakdown makes the time feel fair.

situation: Disagreeing with a deadline someone set
mightSay: This deadline is impossible, nobody can do this.
better: I don't think we can do it well by Friday. Wednesday next week is realistic.

next.title: Give a choice

lines.label: Choice
lines.text: Or by Friday with only the main screen ready.

next.note: Trade scope for time, out loud.

situation: Saying no to a sales call
mightSay: Not interested, don't call again.
better: Thanks, but I'm not interested. Please take my number off your list.

next.title: If they push

lines.label: Again
lines.text: I've decided. Thank you for your time.

next.note: Repeat the same line, calmly.

situation: Asking someone to explain again
mightSay: I didn't understand anything, tell again.
better: Sorry, could you explain the last step again? I missed how the totals add up.

next.title: Check you understood

lines.label: Repeat
lines.text: So the tax is added after the discount. Is that right?

next.note: Saying it back shows what you got.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a password reset to an elder
mightSay: Click on forgot password, then OTP will come, enter it and reset.
better: Tap 'Forgot password'. You'll get a code by text. Type it in, then choose a new password.

next.title: Add a safety line

lines.label: Warn
lines.text: Never tell that code to anyone who calls you.

next.note: Short steps and one warning are easy to remember.

situation: Disagreeing with a colleague's estimate
mightSay: Your estimate is wrong, it will take much more time.
better: I think it may take longer. Testing alone took us a week last time.

next.title: Suggest a buffer

lines.label: Buffer
lines.text: Could we say three weeks, to be safe?

next.note: Past work is a fair judge.

situation: Saying no to a new project while you're full
mightSay: I am already overloaded, how can I take more?
better: I'd like to help, but I'm full until the 20th. Which task should I drop to take this on?

next.title: Offer a date

lines.label: Date
lines.text: I could start on it on the 21st.

next.note: Let your manager pick the priority.

situation: Asking for a reference letter
mightSay: Sir, please give me one reference letter, it is urgent.
better: Would you be willing to write me a reference for a project manager role? It's due on the 15th.

next.title: Make it easy

lines.label: Help
lines.text: I can send a short list of projects we did together.

next.note: Give them the facts so they can write it quickly.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining AI to your grandparents
mightSay: AI is machine learning models trained on huge datasets to predict outputs.
better: AI is a computer program that has read a lot and can answer questions in plain words.

next.title: Show it working

lines.label: Try
lines.text: Ask it: 'What can I cook with potatoes?' and see.

next.note: Let them try one thing.

situation: Disagreeing about who owns a task
mightSay: This is not my work, it is your team's work.
better: I think this sits with the data team. Can we check with Priya and confirm?

next.title: Offer to help

lines.label: Help
lines.text: Once it's clear, I'm happy to hand over my notes.

next.note: Settle it with a fact, not a fight.

situation: Saying no to staying late
mightSay: I can't stay, I have to go, sorry sorry.
better: I need to leave at 6 today. I'll finish this first thing tomorrow.

next.title: If it can't wait

lines.label: Option
lines.text: If it's urgent, I can send you my part before I go.

next.note: Give a time, not an apology.

situation: Asking a neighbour to collect a parcel
mightSay: Please take my parcel, I am not there.
better: Hi, I'm out on Thursday. Could you collect a parcel for me if it comes?

next.title: Thank them

lines.label: Thanks
lines.text: Thank you, I'll pick it up from you in the evening.

next.note: Say how long it will stay with them.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining what testing is
mightSay: Testing is QA process for validating functional and non-functional requirements.
better: Testing means we use the app the way you would, to catch problems before you do.

next.title: Give an example

lines.label: Example
lines.text: We tried paying with an expired card to make sure it shows a clear message.

next.note: One real check makes it concrete.

situation: Saying the job is done, without 'done the needful'
mightSay: I have done the needful, kindly check.
better: I've updated the address in the system. Please check it's right.

next.title: Even better

lines.label: Specific
lines.text: I've updated your address. Your next bill will go to the new one.

next.note: 'Done the needful' hides what you actually did.

situation: Disagreeing with a design choice
mightSay: This design is not looking good, change it.
better: I like the layout. The grey text is hard to read on a phone, though.

next.title: Suggest a fix

lines.label: Try
lines.text: Could we try darker text and see?

next.note: Name the problem; let the designer pick the fix.

situation: Saying no to a trip with friends
mightSay: I'll see, I'm not sure, let me check and tell.
better: I'll skip this one, but have a great time. Send pictures!

next.title: Plan another

lines.label: Next
lines.text: I'd love to join the next one. Maybe in March?

next.note: A quick no lets them plan.

situation: Asking for advice on a career move
mightSay: Should I leave my job or not? Tell me what to do.
better: I've got an offer from a startup. Could I get your view on the risks?
changes: ask for a view, not a decision

next.title: Ask a sharp question

lines.label: Question
lines.text: What would you check before joining a startup?

next.note: A specific question gets a useful answer.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a security risk to your boss
mightSay: There is a vulnerability in our system which can be exploited by hackers.
better: Anyone with our old password can still open the customer list. We should change it today.

next.title: Give the cost

lines.label: Cost
lines.text: It takes one hour. A leak could cost us our biggest client.

next.note: Compare the small fix to the big risk.

situation: Disagreeing without saying 'but'
mightSay: Good idea, but it won't work.
better: Good idea. And if we try it, we'll need a bigger budget.

next.title: Solve it together

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: How could we make the budget work?

next.note: 'But' cancels what came before it.

situation: Saying no to a colleague's shortcut
mightSay: No, we can't do like this, it is wrong method.
better: I'd rather not skip the review. If something breaks, it's on both of us.

next.title: Offer a faster way

lines.label: Option
lines.text: I can review it in an hour, so we still make the deadline.

next.note: Keep the goal; change the method.

situation: Asking for help without sounding helpless
mightSay: I am not able to do anything, I am totally lost.
better: I've done the first half. I need help with the formula in step 3.

next.title: Ask for the right amount

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: Ten minutes on a call would do it.

next.note: Progress plus one gap sounds capable.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining an API to a business partner
mightSay: API is an interface through which two systems communicate with each other.
better: Our app can send orders straight to your system, so no one has to type them in.

next.title: Name the benefit

lines.label: Benefit
lines.text: That saves your team about two hours a day.

next.note: Talk about the result, not the tech.

situation: Disagreeing in writing
mightSay: As per my last mail, I already told this is incorrect.
better: I think the figure in row 4 may be off. Could you check it against the March report?

next.title: Keep the door open

lines.label: Close
lines.text: Happy to talk it through if that's easier.

next.note: In writing, softer words read as normal.

situation: Saying no to a discount request
mightSay: Sorry, we can't give discount, rate is fixed.
better: This is our best price. I can add free delivery, though.

next.title: If they push

lines.label: Option
lines.text: For a yearly order, I can do 5% off.

next.note: Trade a discount for something you want.

situation: Asking for help early, not at the deadline
mightSay: Deadline is today and I am still not finished, please help.
better: I'm behind on the report due Friday. Could we talk today about what to cut?

next.title: Show your plan

lines.label: Plan
lines.text: I can finish the numbers. I need help with the charts.

next.note: Early asks give people room to help.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a server outage to customers
mightSay: Due to technical issue in server, services were down.
better: Our app was down for two hours this morning. It's working again now.

next.title: Say sorry and what's next

lines.label: Next
lines.text: We're sorry. We've added a backup so this is less likely to happen again.

next.note: Customers want to know what, how long, and that it's fixed.

situation: Disagreeing with a senior in public
mightSay: Sir, with respect, you are wrong in this point.
better: Can I add one thing? Last quarter's numbers point the other way.

next.title: Take the rest offline

lines.label: Offer
lines.text: I can send you the figures after the meeting.

next.note: Let them save face in front of others.

situation: Saying no to a promotion you don't want
mightSay: I don't want this post, please give to someone else.
better: Thank you for thinking of me. I'd like to stay hands-on for now.

next.title: Leave room for later

lines.label: Later
lines.text: Could we talk about it again next year?

next.note: Turn a no into a career plan.

situation: Asking a teammate to check your numbers
mightSay: Just check my sheet once, I think it is fine.
better: Could you check the totals in my budget sheet? A second look would really help.

next.title: Point to the risky part

lines.label: Focus
lines.text: I'm least sure about the tax column.

next.note: Point them to the spot that worries you.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a budget spreadsheet to family
mightSay: Column B is inflow, column C is outflow, and D is the net balance.
better: This column is what comes in, this one is what we spend, and this shows what's left.

next.title: Show the answer

lines.label: Point
lines.text: This number at the bottom is what we can save each month.

next.note: Lead them to the one number that matters.

situation: Disagreeing with a relative's advice
mightSay: Aunty, your thinking is old, things are different now.
better: Thank you, I know you care. I've thought about it, and I'd like to try it my way.

next.title: Keep them close

lines.label: Add
lines.text: I'll tell you how it goes.

next.note: You can disagree and still keep the warmth.

situation: Saying no to a party on a weeknight
mightSay: Weekday party? No way, I have office tomorrow.
better: I'll pass tonight, I've got an early start. Have fun!

next.title: Suggest another time

lines.label: Option
lines.text: I'm free on Saturday, if anyone's up for it.

next.note: Short and cheerful works with friends.

situation: Asking HR about leave rules
mightSay: What is the leave policy? Please explain all the rules.
better: Could you tell me how many days of leave I can carry into next year?

next.title: Add your case

lines.label: Context
lines.text: I have eight days left and I'm planning a trip in January.

next.note: Your own case gets a direct answer.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining what you built this month
mightSay: I worked on many tickets and did refactoring and bug fixes.
better: This month I made checkout faster. Orders now go through in half the time.

next.title: Add what's next

lines.label: Next
lines.text: Next month I'll fix the search page.

next.note: Lead with the result people can feel.

situation: Disagreeing on a hiring choice
mightSay: That candidate is not good, I don't like him.
better: I'd go with the second candidate. She has done this exact job before.

next.title: Name your concern

lines.label: Concern
lines.text: The first one was strong, but he's never managed a team.

next.note: Compare them on the job, not as people.

situation: Saying no to free work for a friend's business
mightSay: Actually these days I am very busy, so it will be difficult for me.
better: I'd love to see your business grow, but I can't take on free work right now.

next.title: Offer smaller help

lines.label: Option
lines.text: I can give you an hour of advice next week.

next.note: A small free help keeps the friendship.

situation: Asking a client for missing details
mightSay: You have not sent all the details, so we cannot start.
better: To start, we just need two things: your logo and the delivery address.

next.title: Add a date

lines.label: Date
lines.text: If we get them by Wednesday, we'll deliver on time.

next.note: Link the ask to what they want.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a cost estimate to a client
mightSay: The total cost is ₹4 lakh as per our estimation.
better: It's ₹4 lakh: ₹3 lakh to build and ₹1 lakh for testing and setup.

next.title: Show a cheaper choice

lines.label: Option
lines.text: Without the phone app, it's ₹3 lakh.

next.note: A breakdown makes a price feel fair.

situation: Disagreeing with a vendor's price
mightSay: Your rate is too high, reduce it.
better: Your quote is higher than the others we've had. Can you do better on price?

next.title: Give a number

lines.label: Target
lines.text: We can sign this week at ₹50,000.

next.note: A clear target speeds things up.

situation: Saying no to your boss, with an option
mightSay: Not possible, I have too much already.
better: I can't do both by Friday. I can do the report now and the deck on Monday.

next.title: Let them choose

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: Or which one matters more this week?

next.note: Your boss sets the priority; you give the facts.

situation: Asking for feedback on a draft
mightSay: Please see my draft and give comments.
better: Could you read my draft and tell me if the main point is clear?

next.title: Give a time

lines.label: Time
lines.text: It's one page. Any time before Thursday is fine.

next.note: A clear question gets better feedback.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining backups to a small shop owner
mightSay: You need regular backups with offsite storage for disaster recovery.
better: Every night, a copy of your sales records goes online. If the computer breaks, nothing is lost.

next.title: Say the cost

lines.label: Cost
lines.text: It costs ₹300 a month.

next.note: Owners decide on cost and risk.

situation: Disagreeing with a teammate's priority
mightSay: Why are you doing this first? That one is more important.
better: I'd put the payment bug first. It's stopping customers from paying.

next.title: Ask their reason

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: What made you pick the report first?

next.note: They might know something you don't.

situation: Saying no and offering a later date
mightSay: This week not possible.
better: I can't this week, but I can do next Tuesday.

next.title: Even better

lines.label: Specific
lines.text: Next Tuesday at 2 works. Shall I send an invite?

next.note: A date in the no makes it a yes for later.

situation: Asking a friend to read your CV
mightSay: Check my CV and tell me, is it good or not?
better: Could you read my CV? I'd love to know if my last job sounds strong enough.

next.title: Thank them

lines.label: Thanks
lines.text: Coffee's on me this weekend!

next.note: A focused ask is quicker for them.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining why the app needs an update
mightSay: Update is mandatory because of security patches and compatibility.
better: This update fixes a safety problem and keeps the app working on new phones.

next.title: Say how long

lines.label: Time
lines.text: It takes about two minutes.

next.note: People update faster when they know it's quick.

situation: Disagreeing after you first agreed
mightSay: Sorry, earlier I said yes but actually I don't agree.
better: I've thought more about it, and I've changed my mind. Here's why.

next.title: Give the reason

lines.label: Reason
lines.text: The new numbers show it will cost twice what we thought.

next.note: Changing your mind with a reason sounds thoughtful.

situation: Saying no to taking notes again
mightSay: Why always me? Someone else take notes.
better: I've taken notes the last three times. Could we rotate?

next.title: Suggest a system

lines.label: System
lines.text: Maybe we take turns, in alphabetical order?

next.note: A system is easier to agree to than a complaint.

situation: Asking for an introduction
mightSay: You know Mr. Rao, no? Please connect me to him.
better: Would you be comfortable introducing me to Mr. Rao? I'd like to ask him about the logistics role.

next.title: Make it easy

lines.label: Help
lines.text: I can send a short note you can forward.

next.note: Make the introduction one click for them.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining why you can't have both fast and cheap
mightSay: Sir, you can't get everything, fast and cheap both is not possible.
better: We can do it fast or we can do it cheap. Doing both means cutting quality.

next.title: Show the options

lines.label: Options
lines.text: Fast: ₹6 lakh in a month. Cheaper: ₹4 lakh in three months.

next.note: Put numbers on each choice.

situation: Pointing out a mistake in a slide
mightSay: Your slide is having a mistake.
better: Quick one: slide 5 says 2023, but I think it's 2024.

next.title: Say it privately

lines.label: Message
lines.text: Spotted a typo on slide 5. Want me to fix it?

next.note: A private message saves them embarrassment.

situation: Saying no to a team outing
mightSay: I won't come, team outings are boring.
better: I'll miss this one, I have a family plan. Have a great time!

next.title: Show you're still in

lines.label: Add
lines.text: Count me in for the next lunch.

next.note: Keep the door open to the team.

situation: Asking for a quick call to get unstuck
mightSay: Can we connect? I have some doubts.
better: Could we do a 10-minute call today? I'm stuck on how to price the add-ons.

next.title: Offer times

lines.label: Times
lines.text: I'm free at 12 or after 4.

next.note: Busy people say yes to short calls.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining two-step login to a parent
mightSay: Two-factor authentication adds an extra layer of security.
better: After your password, the bank sends a code to your phone. Only you can see it.

next.title: Add the rule

lines.label: Rule
lines.text: If you didn't try to log in, ignore the code and tell me.

next.note: One rule protects them from scams.

situation: Announcing an earlier date, without 'preponed'
mightSay: The meeting has been preponed to Monday.
better: The meeting has moved earlier, to Monday.

next.title: Even better

lines.label: Specific
lines.text: We've moved the meeting earlier, to Monday at 10. Does that work?

next.note: 'Prepone' is mostly used in India; 'bring forward' works everywhere.

situation: Questioning a decision made without you
mightSay: Why nobody asked me before deciding this?
better: I saw the decision on vendors. I'd like to share a concern before we sign.

next.title: Ask for next time

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: Could I be in the loop on vendor choices from now on?

next.note: Fix this one, then fix the process.

situation: Saying no to a volunteering request
mightSay: Sorry, no time for all this.
better: Thank you for asking. I can't commit this month.

next.title: Offer something small

lines.label: Option
lines.text: I can share the poster on my page.

next.note: A small yes softens a big no.

situation: Asking for help in a group chat
mightSay: Anyone? Urgent help needed!!!
better: Does anyone know how to export the client list from the CRM? I need it by 3.

next.title: Thank and close

lines.label: Close
lines.text: Got it, thanks Ravi!

next.note: Close the loop so others know it's solved.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining what a product manager does
mightSay: PM owns the roadmap and drives cross-functional alignment.
better: I decide what the app should do next, and make sure the team builds it well.

next.title: Add an example

lines.label: Example
lines.text: This month I chose to add a dark mode, because users asked for it most.

next.note: One real decision explains the job.

situation: Disagreeing with a friend's travel plan
mightSay: Goa in May? Are you mad? It will be too hot.
better: Goa in May might be very hot. What about Shimla instead?

next.title: Leave it open

lines.label: Add
lines.text: But if you're set on Goa, I'm in.

next.note: Suggest, then let them choose.

situation: Saying no to a neighbour's favour
mightSay: Sorry aunty, I am not free, maybe some other time.
better: I'm sorry, I can't water the plants this week. I'm travelling too.

next.title: Help find someone

lines.label: Option
lines.text: Maybe the Mehtas upstairs could help?

next.note: Point them to someone who can.

situation: Asking a parent for advice
mightSay: Mummy, tell me what to do, I am confused.
better: Mum, can I ask your advice? I'm choosing between two flats.

next.title: Share the details

lines.label: Details
lines.text: One is closer to work. The other is bigger and cheaper.

next.note: Give them the facts so they can help.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining automation to an office team
mightSay: We are implementing automation to optimise manual workflows.
better: The system will fill in the daily report for you, so you won't have to copy numbers.

next.title: Answer the worry

lines.label: Reassure
lines.text: Your job stays. You'll just spend less time copying.

next.note: People worry first about their jobs.

situation: Partly agreeing, then adding your view
mightSay: Yes but no, I partially agree only.
better: I agree on the timeline. On the budget, I see it differently.

next.title: Explain the difference

lines.label: Reason
lines.text: We'll need about 20% more for testing.

next.note: Agreement first makes the rest easier to hear.

situation: Saying no to a request outside your role
mightSay: This is not my job.
better: That's outside my area. Leela in finance handles refunds.

next.title: Help a bit

lines.label: Offer
lines.text: I can copy her on this email now.

next.note: Passing it on well still sounds helpful.

situation: Asking someone busy for five minutes
mightSay: Are you free? I want to talk to you.
better: When you have five minutes today, could I ask you about the new contract?

next.title: Be ready

lines.label: Prepare
lines.text: I'll have my two questions ready.

next.note: Prepared asks stay short.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a chart to someone who hates numbers
mightSay: As you can see, Y-axis is revenue and X-axis is months, and there is a positive trend.
better: In short: sales have gone up every month since January.

next.title: Add one number

lines.label: Number
lines.text: We've doubled since January.

next.note: One number is enough for most people.

situation: Saying you see it differently, with a reason
mightSay: I have a different opinion.
better: I see it differently. Our customers are mostly over 50, so the app has to stay simple.

next.title: Invite a reply

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: Does that change anything for you?

next.note: A reason turns an opinion into a point.

situation: Saying no to an unpaid trial task
mightSay: I cannot do so much work for free, sir.
better: I'm happy to do a short task. For anything over two hours, I'd need to be paid.

next.title: Offer another proof

lines.label: Option
lines.text: I can share samples of similar work instead.

next.note: Protect your time without losing the chance.

situation: Asking for help after a mistake
mightSay: Something went wrong, I don't know how it happened.
better: I sent the wrong file to the client. Could you help me fix it before they open it?

next.title: Show your plan

lines.label: Plan
lines.text: I'll email them now. Can you check my message?

next.note: Own it fast and come with a plan.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining online payment safety to an elder
mightSay: Never share OTP, CVV, PIN with anyone, it is a scam.
better: The bank will never ask for your code on a call. If someone does, hang up.

next.title: Add one check

lines.label: Check
lines.text: Before paying, look for the lock sign next to the website name.

next.note: One rule at a time is easy to remember.

situation: Disagreeing with a landlord about repairs
mightSay: This repair is your responsibility, I won't pay.
better: The leak was there before I moved in. I think the repair should be on you.

next.title: Point to the agreement

lines.label: Proof
lines.text: The agreement says major repairs are the owner's cost. I can send photos.

next.note: Facts and photos settle it calmly.

situation: Saying no without a long excuse
mightSay: Actually what happened is, my cousin is coming and then I have one function and also...
better: I can't make it, sorry. Thanks for asking.

next.title: Add warmth

lines.label: Add
lines.text: Hope it goes really well!

next.note: Long excuses sound less true, not more.

situation: Asking for training
mightSay: I don't know Excel properly, please send me for training.
better: Could I take an advanced Excel course? It would cut my reporting time in half.

next.title: Make it easy

lines.label: Detail
lines.text: There's a two-day course in May. It costs ₹8,000.

next.note: Give your manager the facts to say yes.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a launch plan to marketing
mightSay: We will do phased rollout with feature flags from Q3.
better: We'll open it to 10% of users in July, then to everyone in August.

next.title: Say what you need

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: Could you have the emails ready by July 1?

next.note: Tell them their part and when.

situation: Disagreeing with a reviewer's comment
mightSay: Your comment is not valid, I have done it correctly.
better: Thanks for the comment. I did it this way to keep it fast. Does that work for you?

next.title: Offer to change

lines.label: Option
lines.text: If you still prefer the other way, I'm happy to change it.

next.note: Explain, then stay open.

situation: Saying no to a meeting with no agenda
mightSay: What is this meeting for? I won't join without knowing.
better: Could you share the agenda? Then I'll know if I'm needed.

next.title: Offer another way

lines.label: Option
lines.text: If it's just an update, I'm happy to read the notes.

next.note: Asking for an agenda is a polite filter.

situation: Asking someone to share the workload
mightSay: I am doing everything alone, you also do something.
better: I've got the report and the client calls this week. Could you take the client calls?

next.title: Offer a swap

lines.label: Return
lines.text: I'll take your Friday review in exchange.

next.note: Make it a fair swap.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining a data report to a client
mightSay: The report has many metrics, please go through all the sheets.
better: The main point: repeat orders rose 15% this quarter. Page 2 shows why.

next.title: Add the next step

lines.label: Next
lines.text: We suggest more loyalty offers next quarter.

next.note: Clients read the first line; make it count.

situation: Disagreeing with a plan everyone likes
mightSay: Everyone is saying yes, but I think it is a bad idea.
better: I like where this is going. Can I argue the other side for a minute?

next.title: Raise the risk

lines.label: Risk
lines.text: If the supplier is late, the whole launch slips.

next.note: Testing a plan helps it, even when everyone agrees.

situation: Saying no to investing in a cousin's business
mightSay: Let me think, I will discuss with family and tell you later.
better: I'm glad you're starting this. I'm not putting money into businesses right now.

next.title: Offer other help

lines.label: Option
lines.text: I can help you write the plan or meet people.

next.note: Support without money is still support.

situation: Asking a shop for a refund
mightSay: This product is defective, give my money back.
better: This kettle stopped working after two days. I'd like a refund, please.

next.title: Have proof ready

lines.label: Proof
lines.text: Here's the bill. I bought it on Saturday.

next.note: Facts and the bill make it quick.

topic: Explaining work to a non-tech person
situation: Explaining why the old system must go
mightSay: Legacy system is not scalable and has a lot of technical debt.
better: The old system crashes on big sales days, and fixing it costs more each year.

next.title: Show the gain

lines.label: Gain
lines.text: The new one handles three times the orders for less money.

next.note: Compare old and new in money and trouble.
